subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What exact private/ephemeral session contract should OpenClaw expose, and which storage, memory, plugin, channel, artifact, diagnostic, and UI surfaces must enforce it before the product can claim Private Mode?
rationale: The requested behavior is a user-facing privacy/security guarantee across core persistence and plugin boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the threat model, protocol shape, or enforcement coverage.

options.title: Design Shared Core Contract
options.body: Define an additive private/ephemeral session marker in core and require every persistence, memory, plugin, channel, and UI surface to enforce or explicitly reject it before advertising Private Mode.

options.title: Narrow To Context Suppression
options.body: Ship only a clearly named context-suppression mode if maintainers want a smaller feature that does not promise no durable history or memory writes.

options.title: Defer And Document Mitigations
options.body: Keep the issue open or defer it while documenting current partial mitigations such as contextInjection and memory controls without claiming private sessions.

recommendation.title: Design Shared Core Contract
recommendation.body: Define an additive private/ephemeral session marker in core and require every persistence, memory, plugin, channel, and UI surface to enforce or explicitly reject it before advertising Private Mode.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session/transcript history plus the prior canonical review make this the strongest available owner for choosing the product and security contract.
